title: yadakchi.review.decided.v1
description:
A human decision. The permanent record of human judgment.

Producers: ops. Consumers: matcher, fitment.
Kafka message key: request_uid — it must be set; compaction and partition ordering depend on it.
Cleanup: compact, retention infinite — human decisions are permanent.

This file validates a whole Kafka message body: the shared envelope from docs/specs/02-EVENT-CONTRACTS.md plus this topic's payload. Unknown fields are ignored, never rejected, at both levels — that is what lets a producer add an optional field without breaking a consumer.

event_id.description: UUIDv4, unique per emission. Two emissions of the same fact carry different event_ids; consumers deduplicate on the payload's natural identity, not on this.

event_type.description: The topic name without the 'yadakchi.' prefix and without the version suffix.

version.description: Envelope and payload version. A removed field, a renamed field or a changed type is a breaking change: publish to .v2 and run both until consumers migrate.

occurred_at.description: When the fact happened, ISO-8601 UTC with Z. Consumers tolerate out-of-order delivery across partitions by comparing this, never by assuming global ordering.

producer.description: The service that emitted this message. Constrained to the producers declared for this topic in platform/kafka/topics.yml.

trace_id.description: Propagated across the whole chain for debugging. Minted by crawler on the listings.observed topic and carried through every derived event; a service starting a chain of its own (a human admin edit, a scheduled recomputation) mints a fresh one. Every service logs it.

payload.description: This topic is never deleted. Human decisions are sticky: after any full reprocess, consumers replay this topic LAST and a human decision overrides everything computed. A tombstone — payload: null with the envelope intact — means this entity is deleted; compaction keeps it as the last word on the key.

request_uid.description: The review.requested this answers. Also the Kafka key.

kind.description: Copied from the request it answers, so a consumer can route the decision without holding the original request.

decision.description: The verdict. same_product and different_products answer a merge_pair; approve, reject and skip answer the rest. For kind 'fitment_conflict' this field says only WHETHER a human settled it — approve means they did and subject.status carries what they settled on, skip means they did not. reject is not used there: it reads as 'incompatible' and would leave no way to record a settled 'unknown'.

subject.description:
What the decision applies to. ops builds it from the request's subject and MAY add or replace keys that only exist once a human has decided — it is not a verbatim copy.

Two parts, and a consumer should read them differently:
  * IDENTIFYING keys are carried through unchanged from the request, so a consumer can apply the decision without holding the original event.
  * VERDICT keys are written by ops and appear only here. For kind 'fitment_conflict' that is `status` — compatible | incompatible | unknown — which carries the settled verdict, because `decision` is shared across every kind and cannot express a tri-state. ops also drops request-only context such as `part_type` that played no part in the decision.

The exact key set per kind is fixed in docs/specs/02-EVENT-CONTRACTS.md. A consumer needing another key raises a contract change rather than inventing it.

actor.description: Who decided. Every mutating action records the actor.

reason.description: Free-text rationale, or null when none was given.
